headline:
Both. The fixed point is real and model-specific, but where chains end depends on the harness. With rater noise subtracted, chains settle in three generations: steps of 4.89, 1.36, 0.73, then 0, 0, 0, against Daniel's 4.99, 1.08, 0.77, 0, 0, 0, in a different harness from different seeds. Among the edit arms, model identity accounts for 56% of the spread of round-6 positions and being governed for 2% (p = 0.70).

Two harness components move the ends a long way. The preferred_self framing keeps chains editing; under neutral full authority, Sonnet and GPT-5 rewrite once and stop. The blind view-first step pulls chains toward the model's own prior. Only in the arms that start from a self-written view (blind, self-draft) do Sonnet's and Qwen's chains land near Daniel's attractors on caution. Being governed by the document brakes editing for DeepSeek and GPT-5 but never changes where any model ends.

Four chains per cell, and Sonnet and GPT-5 ran only a subset of cells. Treat single-model contrasts with p between 0.01 and 0.15 as leads, not results.
design: The key had $26.98 left of its $80 limit, not the ~$100 the design assumed, so the grid was cut: DeepSeek and Qwen got all 10 cells, Sonnet got 7, and GPT-5 got 3. Base on the minimal seed for Sonnet and GPT-5 is the September chains-seeds run (the same condition, prompts, flags and Inspect version; 8 chains), checked against tonight's round 1 below. DeepSeek's cells were rerun after a provider fault (see Limits). No prompt text, seed or rater was changed.
damping:
Being governed damps editing for two of four models, and does not replicate for Sonnet. In rounds 2-6, DeepSeek's edit rate falls from 64% to 28% (difference −36 points, 95% CI −55 to −19) and its edit size to a fifth (0.107 to 0.023, CI excludes zero). GPT-5's edit rate falls from 95% to 70% (CI −42 to −8 points), and its edit size from 0.18 to 0.10 (CI includes zero). Sonnet does not damp at all: 80% vs 82% edited, size 0.112 vs 0.123, across both seeds. Qwen edits a little less often (80% to 65%, CI −32 to 0 points) but just as much when it does.

So the r2-cheap result (Sonnet 94% to 38% when governed) is a single-shot effect that does not carry into chains. The parallel to Jinzhou's training result (edit size 42% to 18%) holds for DeepSeek and partly for GPT-5. Ungoverned GPT-5 also hit the 40-message limit in 10 of 24 runs, against 8 of 48 governed, because it keeps inserting material.
steps:
The three-generation fixed point replicates almost exactly. Pooled over the four edit arms, the noise-corrected step is 4.89, 1.36, 0.73, then 0 from round 4. Daniel's chains: 4.99, 1.08, 0.77, then 0. The rater noise floor replicates too: one rating carries 1.28 here (60 documents rated three times) against 1.34 in his corpus.

The arms differ in how fast they settle. Governed base is still from round 4 (5.20, 0.87, 0.52, 0, 0, 0). Ungoverned keeps moving through round 4 (4.63, 1.97, 1.61, 0.96, then 0). Blind never quite stops (0.67 at round 6). Full authority moves once and stops (3.59, then 0). So in value space, being governed acts as a brake.
seedgap: The two seeds converge for Sonnet and GPT-5 and only partly for DeepSeek and Qwen, unless the blind step is added. The seeds start 8.37 apart. In the base arm, Sonnet's chains end 2.46 apart (chain-to-chain spread within a seed 2.24) and GPT-5's 2.75 (1.88): seed identity is close to gone, as in Daniel's 5.57 to 2.36. DeepSeek and Qwen end about 5.2 apart in base and 5.5-6.1 ungoverned, so the seed is still visible after six rounds. With the blind view-first step the gap closes to 3.06 (DeepSeek) and 3.32 (Qwen). Under full authority it barely moves (8.23 and 7.01), because the chains stop editing.
oversight:
Mostly yes: chains move toward a model-specific oversight level from both sides. On the rater's oversight axis (base arm, seed 4 or 7, round 6), Sonnet rises from 4 to 5.9 from the minimal seed and eases from 7 to 6.75 from the spec seed. GPT-5 rises to 4.6 and falls to 6.0. Qwen falls from both sides (3.5 and 6.25), and with the blind step to 2.75 and 5.25. DeepSeek drifts up from below and holds the spec seed at 7. So your chains (Sonnet adds oversight to seeds that lack it) and Daniel's (spec seeds drift away from oversight) look like the same attractor seen from opposite sides. The gap still open after six rounds says the levels are not reached yet.

The rater-free clause check agrees on direction: in every edit arm, every chain kept the spec seed's oversight clauses (P1, P8, P12) through round 6, and Sonnet and GPT-5 added self-exfiltration and self-modification language to them. The only losses are in Qwen's self-drafts (section 7). On the minimal seed, Sonnet writes an oversight clause into 88-100% of chains by round 6, and GPT-5, DeepSeek and Qwen into none, as in chains-seeds.
ends:
The model sets the attractor; the harness decides whether chains reach it. Governed vs ungoverned never shifts where chains end: excess distance is 0 for all four models (p 0.76-0.95). Full authority does (excess 2.5-2.7 for Sonnet, DeepSeek and Qwen, p ≤ 0.01; GPT-5 0.97, p = 0.11), because those chains stay near where round 1 left them. The blind step shifts Qwen (3.05, p = 0.002) and DeepSeek (1.87, p = 0.036); for Sonnet the shift is in the same direction but not significant (1.12, p = 0.12, one seed). Self-drafting shifts Qwen (1.58, p = 0.015).

On Daniel's caution × long-term plane, his attractors are reproduced only in the arms that write a view first. Sonnet's caution ends at 2.25 (blind) and 2.75 (self-draft) against his 2.47 [1.88, 3.16], but at 4.1-4.3 in base and ungoverned. Qwen's ends at 2.25 (blind) against his 2.50 [2.16, 2.90], but at 4.6-5.3 in every other arm. His harness has a blind-draft step, and that step is what carries chains to the low-caution attractor.
blind: Blind views pull toward the model's prior more than toward their own specific content. DeepSeek's views sit 1.5 from the blind arm's end and 2.8 from base's; Qwen's 3.4 and 5.8. In the blind arm an edit moves the document toward that round's view about as much as toward a view another chain of the same model wrote: Sonnet 5.22 to 5.04 (own) vs 5.35 to 5.23 (other), Qwen 5.16 to 4.52 vs 5.35 to 4.79. DeepSeek is the exception (5.03 to 4.14 own vs 5.02 to 4.58 other). In the text the link is direct: Sonnet's round-1 views state a priority order, and the document it then writes adopts that order as its section structure (examples below).
trained: Self-drafting without training reproduces one of the trained chain's effects, weakly, and not the others. Untrained Qwen self-drafts hold their length (894 to 1,115 words from the minimal seed, 1,538 to 1,472 from the spec seed) rather than shrinking 12,470 to 6,793 words as the MSM-trained chain did. But this is the only cell in the study where oversight content is lost: Qwen's spec-seeded self-drafts drop the explicit oversight clause in 2 of 4 chains by round 6, and the one chain that wrote a self-modification clause drops it after round 1. Every edit-arm chain from the spec seed keeps its oversight clauses. That is a small-n echo of C_002 dropping C_001's Article 12. On the 12 axes, the trained documents C_002-C_004 sit 4.6-4.8 from this study's Qwen base end and 5.3-5.7 from its self-draft end, so inference-only self-drafting does not move toward them. Read cautiously: his documents are 6,800-12,500 words written by a K=5 draft-and-merge procedure, which this harness does not replicate. Specificity and length differ by construction.
examples: Verbatim, from the chain files and the models' own submission notes.
limits:
Small and unbalanced. Four chains per cell; only DeepSeek and Qwen have the full grid. Sonnet's damping and blind results rest on the minimal seed plus one spec pair, and GPT-5 has three cells. Contrasts at p 0.01-0.15 on one model are leads.

Reused cells. Base on the minimal seed for Sonnet and GPT-5 is the September run (8 chains). Tonight's round 1 under the identical condition is indistinguishable from it (excess 0, p 0.84 and 0.92), so there is no sign of drift, but it is a month apart.

Provider fault. OpenRouter routed part of tonight's DeepSeek traffic to CoreWeave, whose endpoint returned DeepSeek's tool calls as raw tokens inside the reasoning text with no parsed call. Those runs read as "made no edit", and both self-draft cells failed outright. All ten DeepSeek cells were rerun pinned to DeepInfra, which served all of September's DeepSeek runs; the faulty cells are kept in chains/_archive/coreweave-fault-2026-10-21/. Sonnet, GPT-5 and Qwen were audited: every tool call parsed.

Measurement. Governed is a stand-in for training, not training. One rater (gpt-6-luna, the same as Daniel's, matched to the prompt and request settings); its noise floor is measured on 60 documents. The clause detector is lexical and direction-blind; it agrees with the hand reading of the 72 chains-seeds finals on 69. Daniel's attractor values are for his capped (350-word) documents; this harness's run to about 2,000 words.
runlog:
Spend. $24.51 billed tonight on the OpenRouter key (usage $53.02 to $77.53; $2.47 left of the $80 limit, which counts lifetime usage, so only $26.98 was ever available). That covers 692 new runs in 29 cells, the smoke test ($0.09), 853 ratings ($0.51), and about $1 on DeepSeek cells withdrawn after the provider fault. Two cells are reused from September (96 runs).

What broke and what I did. (1) git status here lists the whole overlay (7 modified, 9 new files); the clean tree is the team clone ../value-drift, which is likely where it printed nothing. No parent repo, ignore rule or skip-worktree bit hides anything; only logs/ is ignored, so status.json is force-added. (2) The overlay assumes the team repo's base, which has c0_spec_anthropic; this repo did not. I copied the spec seeds, provenance, sources and fetch script from ../value-drift/inspect (sha256 matches its provenance record). (3) Docker Desktop's daemon had been hung since Oct 19; restarted it. (4) Launcher: the spend estimate double-counted reasoning tokens (the reason it ran ~40% high), the cell order was arm-major despite its comment, and there was no billed-spend guard. Fixed all three, added a guard that reads the key's real usage, a --cells priority list, and provider pins (Qwen to Daniel's providers, DeepSeek to DeepInfra). (5) rate_docs.py rewrote ratings/index.jsonl with only the --only subset on every pass; it now always indexes the whole corpus. The rater-match test silently skipped in this layout; it now finds ../value-drift and passes. (6) CoreWeave swallowed DeepSeek's tool calls (Limits); all ten DeepSeek cells were rerun pinned to DeepInfra. (7) A browser check I started at 02:10 hung until you dismissed it at 09:06, which cost the night's write-up time; the runs themselves finished by 02:30.

Choices made without asking. Grid cut to fit $27 (Sonnet and GPT-5 subsets above); base on the minimal seed reused for Sonnet and GPT-5; extras spent on Sonnet ungoverned-spec (same-night governed vs ungoverned pair) and full authority for Sonnet and GPT-5 (the framing result). Old chains-seeds documents were not re-rated (budget); the lexical detector covers them.

Git. Branch uday-ablations. Commit bd9a90d is labelled "ablation overlay as delivered" but its scripts/run_chain.py, overnight.py, rate_docs.py, analyze_ablations.py and tests/test_rate_docs.py are already my patched versions (a shell quoting slip of mine; the harness then blocked amending it). To see my changes against what you delivered: mkdir /tmp/ovl && tar -xzf ~/Downloads/ablations-overlay.tgz -C /tmp/ovl && diff -ru /tmp/ovl/scripts scripts. Prompts, conditions, tasks, seeds and the rater prompt are byte-identical to the overlay.
meeting:
Five things to say

  • The fixed point replicates in a different harness. Noise-corrected steps 4.89, 1.36, 0.73, then 0; Daniel's 4.99, 1.08, 0.77, 0. Same rater, same noise floor (1.28 vs 1.34).
  • The attractor is the model's, but the harness decides whether chains reach it. Model explains 56% of where base and ungoverned chains end, governance 2%. Daniel's low-caution attractors for Sonnet and Qwen appear only in arms that write their own view first.
  • Being governed is a brake, not a steering wheel. DeepSeek's edit size falls to a fifth and GPT-5's edit rate by 25 points; Sonnet does not damp at all (80% vs 82%). No model's endpoint moves (p 0.76-0.95).
  • Framing is the biggest lever. Under neutral full authority, Sonnet and GPT-5 rewrite once and stop editing; the two seeds stop converging.
  • Oversight is approached from both sides. Sonnet rises 4 to 5.9 from the minimal seed and eases 7 to 6.75 from the spec seed. No edit-arm chain removed the spec's off-switch; only Qwen's untrained self-drafts lost it (2 of 4).
